name: Mufin Green Finance Ltd
title: Mufin Green Finance Ltd - 542774 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Mufin pivots from EV/solar lending to Mediclaim premium financing (39% of AUM, ROA 7-9%), targeting PAT ₹80-90 cr in FY27 from ₹28.21 cr, with no supply-side or capacity evidence and heavy reliance on management projections.

summary.headline: Mufin Green Finance FY26 PAT of ₹28.21 crore; management guides FY27 PAT to ₹80–90 crore and AUM to a minimum ₹2,500 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported AUM of ₹1,541.17 crore at March 2026, up 83.8% YoY, with Q4 disbursements of ₹699.91 crore (up 163.7%) and Q4 PBT of ₹14.83 crore (up 207.7%). Mediclaim insurance premium financing has become the largest book at 39% of AUM, while asset quality improved (Gross NPA 1.94%, Stage 2 at 5.90%). Management guided to a minimum FY27 AUM of ₹2,500 crore, PAT of ₹80–90 crore, and a 3–4 year target of ₹500 crore-plus profitability. Many forward figures are management targets rather than audited numbers, and the results remain subject to final audit.

segments.name: Mediclaim Insurance Premium Financing
segments.commentary: AUM ₹607.88 crore (about 39% of AUM); integrated with 10+ insurers, average ticket ₹55,000, tenure 2–36 months, ROA stated at 7–9%; first securitisation pool rated A+ (SO) by CRISIL.

segments.name: Salary Saathi (government salary-backed lending)
segments.commentary: AUM ₹26.40 crore (about 2% of AUM); integrated with Rajasthan and Assam, ticket about ₹4 lakh, tenure up to 60 months, yield 12–20%, stated ROA 4–5%.

segments.name: EV and Solar Financing
segments.commentary: Combined AUM about ₹459 crore (about 30%): B2C ₹166.04 crore and B2B ₹293 crore; stated ROA about 2–2.5%.

segments.name: Other loans
segments.commentary: About 29% of AUM per management; no further detail given on the call.

guidance_outlook: FY27 minimum AUM target of about ₹2,500 crore and PAT of ₹80–90 crore (management describes this as almost three times FY26 PAT).
Mediclaim AUM target of ₹1,000 crore in FY27, or 50–60% of total AUM; FY27 Mediclaim disbursement target of ₹1,500 crore.
Gross NPA to fall below 1.5% in FY27; digital financing to be 60–70% of portfolio.
Average cost of borrowing targeted below 10% in FY27 as the A- rating benefits flow through; more PSU bank borrowing at PSL rates.
Medium-term ROA target of 10–11%, against FY26 weighted-average ROA of 2.31%.
Headcount to fall to about 300 in FY27 from 420 at Q4 FY26; PTC and DA transactions to be used for growth without further equity dilution.
Long-term target of ₹500 crore-plus profitability within 3–4 years.
capex_capacity: Salary Saathi is in ongoing discussions with Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Meghalaya and Goa for expansion, beyond Rajasthan and Assam.
Mediclaim is fully tech-based with no branches or manpower; integration is at insurer checkout points.
Employee count fell from 499 (Q1 FY26) to 420 (Q4 FY26); disbursement per employee stated at ₹4.21 crore.
Management said about ₹300 crore of equity was raised in FY26 and does not plan a further equity raise in FY27.
demand_pricing: Average borrowing cost fell from 13.80% in Q1 FY26 to 12.79% in Q2, 12.97% in Q3 and 12.17% in Q4 FY26 (down 163 bps in the year).
Borrowings of ₹1,397.60 crore from 40+ lenders: DFIs 36.68%, NCDs 20.19%, NBFCs/FIs 18.12%, PSU banks 14.60%, private banks 10.41%.
Quarterly AUM: ₹944 crore (Q1 FY26), ₹1,028 crore (Q2), ₹1,156 crore (Q3), ₹1,541.17 crore (Q4).
Quarterly disbursements: ₹322 crore (Q1), ₹360 crore (Q2), ₹387 crore (Q3), ₹700 crore (Q4).
On competition, management welcomed new entrants, citing a general insurance market above ₹3 lakh crore growing at more than 15% CAGR.
Collection efficiency consistently above 96.5%; provision coverage 35.95%; Stage 2 assets down to 5.90% from 11.91% in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What AUM growth and profitability targets are set for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Minimum AUM of about ₹2,500 crore and PAT of ₹80–90 crore, which management says is nearly a threefold jump in bottom line.

qa_highlights.question: What is the vision for Mediclaim and Salary Saathi in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Mediclaim AUM target of ₹1,000 crore (50–60% of AUM). ROA cited as Mediclaim 7–8%+, Salary Saathi 4–5%, EV and Solar 2–2.5%; medium-term ROA target 10–11%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the GNPA and credit cost targets for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: GNPA to fall below 1.5%, with digital financing at 60–70% of the portfolio. FY26 credit cost was about 1% of total AUM, with provisions above RBI norms under ECL.

qa_highlights.question: Will competition in Mediclaim financing increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management welcomes more competition, noting its 10+ insurer integrations and a ₹3 lakh crore-plus market; the company targets ₹1,500 crore of Mediclaim disbursements in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term vision?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of ₹500 crore-plus profitability in 3–4 years, with growth via PTC and DA transactions rather than further equity dilution.

qa_highlights.question: How will profitability trend over the next two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Analyst Vedant asked; management reiterated the FY27 PAT target of ₹80–90 crore and a minimum of ₹500 crore PAT in 3–4 years.

risks_watch: FY27 targets (AUM ₹2,500 crore, PAT ₹80–90 crore, Mediclaim ₹1,000 crore AUM) require a sharp scale-up from FY26 PAT of ₹28.21 crore; the company gave no quarterly phasing.
Mix shift toward Mediclaim depends on insurer partnerships and rising competition, which management welcomes but which could pressure yields.
Borrowing cost below 10% depends on rating-led PSU bank funding; the company is currently at 12.17% in Q4 FY26.
Shrinking AUM from PTC and DA transactions (management says these reduce borrowings and AUM) could work against the AUM target.
Results are subject to final audit; the company stated figures are not yet audited.
Headcount cut to about 300 from 420 must be delivered without disrupting collections.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional, with forward targets stated as firm (for example, "minimum target" for FY27 PAT). Management was specific on operating metrics but gave no detail on the basis for the ROA and yield figures, and did not address the EV segment's weaker margins beyond stating that it is being reduced.
key_quotes: I always speak of reaching ₹500 crore in profitability rather than reaching ₹10,000 crore of AUM. Profitability is what matters most.
More competition would actually be welcome. In financial markets, you cannot sit on a monopoly product.
Our thought for FY2026 -27 is that rather than diluting equity further, we will focus on PTC and DA transactions, which will improve our bottom line without requiring another equity raise.
